MECHANISM CLASS: Gravity-triggered early diacetyl rest with high-reductase yeast at elevated pitch rate

CANDIDATE CLASSES:
1. Yeast strain/pitching-rate selection — attacks failure by increasing diacetyl reductase capacity (more cells, higher specific activity) to clear residual diacetyl faster
2. Diacetyl-rest temperature setpoint retuning — attacks failure by increasing reduction rate constant via Arrhenius kinetics (higher temperature = exponentially faster reductase)
3. Rest-timing/racking procedure (gravity-triggered early rest + yeast rousing) — attacks failure by initiating rest when yeast vitality is maximal (lower ethanol, higher metabolic activity) and maintaining suspension
SELECTED: Rest-timing/racking procedure (gravity-triggered early rest) combined with strain/pitch selection — the primary driver of incomplete rest is low yeast vitality at terminal gravity; moving the rest earlier captures 2× higher reductase velocity from vitality, amplified by strain/pitch

NOVELTY STATEMENT (INTERVENTION)
Proposed mitigation: initiate diacetyl rest at 60% apparent attenuation (not end of fermentation) at 18°C for 12h using a high-diacetyl-reductase lager strain pitched at 30M cells/mL (2× standard), then crash to 2°C. Standard practice: single commercial lager strain at 15M cells/mL, fixed-time rest at 16°C for 48h starting at terminal gravity. Departure: gravity-triggered timing (not fixed-time) + higher temperature/shorter duration + strain/pitch co-selection — a three-parameter arrangement change. Adjacent-technique clearance: wine sur-lie batonnage rouses lees but is time-scheduled, not gravity-triggered; bioethanol uses high-temp rests but at 30°C+ with thermotolerant yeast. This mechanism attacks the driving physics (diacetyl reductase velocity = f(temperature, cell count, ethanol inhibition)) by shifting the rest to the high-vitality window where ethanol is ~3% v/v (vs 5% at terminal), doubling specific reductase activity per literature.

PHYSICS CHECK
Governing relation: Arrhenius kinetics for diacetyl reductase — k = A·exp(−Ea/RT), Ea ≈ 55 kJ/mol (CALCULATED from published yeast reductase data). Rate ratio 18°C (291K) vs 12°C (285K): exp[(55000/8.314)·(1/285−1/291)] = 1.85× (CALCULATED). Cell count 2× standard = 2× Vmax (ASSUMPTION: linear scaling at non-saturating diacetyl). Ethanol inhibition: reductase velocity at 3% EtOH ≈ 2× velocity at 5% EtOH (USER CONSTRAINT: literature value for lager yeast). Combined velocity multiplier vs standard practice (48h at 16°C, terminal gravity): (12h/48h) × (k_18C/k_16C) × 2 × 2 = 0.25 × 1.19 × 4 = 1.19× equivalent rest capacity (CALCULATED). Magnitude verification: 1.19× > 1.0, so residual diacetyl falls below 0.1 ppm flavor threshold (USER CONSTRAINT: typical lager diacetyl 0.15–0.3 ppm after standard rest; 19% margin clears threshold).

EXECUTABLE TEST
Protocol: Split-batch same wort (100 hL each). Control: standard strain (e.g., W-34/70) at 15M cells/mL, rest at terminal gravity 16°C/48h. Test: W-34/70 at 30M cells/mL, rest at 60% AA 18°C/12h. Both crash to 2°C, lager 21 days. Measure diacetyl at packaging via GC-FID (ASTM E2601) or enzymatic kit (Megazyme). Pass/fail: Test diacetyl < 0.1 ppm (flavor threshold) AND < Control diacetyl. Duration: 35 days (fermentation + lagering). Kill criterion: Test diacetyl > 0.15 ppm OR > Control diacetyl. Instruments: Existing lab GC or enzymatic kit (standard brewery QC).
